scores.evidence: hosted LLM, hosted embeddings, pgvector in existing Postgres... pgvector table with an HNSW index... keyword search merged with reciprocal-rank fusion
scores.rationale: Claims about pgvector/HNSW, hybrid RRF search, pinned model snapshots, DPA/no-training terms via cloud provider endpoints, and blue/green reindexing are all accurate; only trivial imprecision (temperature-0 determinism) with no design consequence.

scores.evidence: Version 1 answers questions only from published, public articles... Account actions and tools... Pull forward when the top unresolved request types are actions
scores.rationale: Solves exactly the stated problem, resolves ambiguities (public-only v1, read-only, no account data) with explicit, justified deferrals and a credible build-vs-buy decision, and is clearly buildable by a small team.

scores.evidence: One serving service (API, retrieval and LLM call in one process) plus one separate ingestion job
scores.rationale: Clear component ownership, a single answer contract and chunk data contract that every consumer reads, and the availability choice is honored consistently (serve last good index, degraded fallbacks); no contradictions found.

scores.evidence: About 150 real questions taken from ticket and search logs... Include ~30 unanswerable questions and ~20 injection cases. Run on every pull request.
scores.rationale: Eval harness is built before the full corpus or launch, every phase has measurable exit checks, agent-assist precedes public exposure, and regression gates plus production feedback continue validation after launch.

scores.evidence: Assumptions (I don't know your stack, so check these first)... If any of these are wrong, the gates in §2 are the first thing to revisit.
scores.rationale: Assumptions are explicit and reasonable, numbers are labeled as 'starting numbers to tune', and every major decision carries a revisit trigger stating what would change the design and how it will be detected.

scores.evidence: The bot confidently states a policy that doesn't exist (for example, promising a refund) as if the company said it.
scores.rationale: Covers the domain's hardest failures — hallucinated commitments, injected docs, stale/deleted content, ingestion failure, LLM outage, Redis loss, poisoned feedback, duplicates via idempotency — each with concrete detection and recovery.

scores.evidence: feature flag, percentage rollout and a kill switch... Kill switch falls back to plain search plus 'contact us'... On-call runbook.
scores.rationale: Deploy/rollback, blue/green index migration, domain-meaningful signals (freshness lag, faithfulness, abstain rate, cost per resolved conversation) and alerting are designed in from day zero at a burden plausible for a small team; only explicit incident ownership is thin.

scores.evidence: ≤ 8k input and ≤ 1k output tokens per turn. ≤ $0.05 per conversation... These are starting numbers to tune against your volume.
scores.rationale: Inference is correctly treated as the dominant cost with concrete controls (caps, routing, rate limits, cost-per-request metrics, buy-vs-build and self-host triggers), but there is no grounded estimate of total run cost, volume, or engineering effort.

scores.evidence: Fix the response format... so it's the most expensive thing to change later... Pin one embedding model... Swap it with a blue/green index rebuild.
scores.rationale: Hard-to-reverse choices (answer contract, chunk schema, embedding model) get the most care with explicit exit paths (provider abstraction, buy option, blue/green rebuild), while reversible choices are decided quickly with revisit triggers.

scores.evidence: A fixed four-step chain (rewrite → retrieve → answer → verify), the simplest shape that works.
scores.rationale: A monolith on existing Postgres with no agent loops, reranker/microservices/fine-tuning explicitly deferred behind measured triggers — the simplest design that still includes all essentials, with a clear growth path.

scores.evidence: Phase 0 — First end-to-end slice... Depends on: nothing beyond existing infra. Exit check: A real question returns a real cited answer in prod.
scores.rationale: Dependency-justified phase ordering, specific schemas and formats, concrete first steps, checkable exit criteria per phase, and stated adaptation paths (revisit triggers) mean a team could start immediately.

checklist.evidence: A full sync plus incremental updates (webhook, or a poll every 10 min)... Unpublishing or deleting an article removes its chunks.
Chunking: split by headings, ~300–500 tokens per chunk... doc_id, chunk_id, version, url, locale, visibility, updated_at, heading_path, text
About 150 real questions taken from ticket and search logs, each mapped to the article(s) that should answer it... Run on every pull request.
answer only from the supplied chunks. Otherwise set answerable=false and hand off... every cited chunk_id must be in the retrieved set.
answers that promise refunds, credits or legal positions get blocked or rewritten into a handoff... creates a ticket with the transcript
Retrieved docs and user text go in delimited data blocks... There are no tools in v1, so the allow-list is empty.
Index public articles only... Visibility filter enforced at query time... needs per-user access control in retrieval and a privacy review
Chat text counts as PII: redact it before logging, keep it 30 days... so we get a data-processing agreement and no-training terms
Read-only. The bot answers and hands off. It never refunds, edits accounts or makes promises.
Thumbs, handoff outcomes and agent edits flow into a review queue... a doc-gap report goes to the content team... Deflection, handoff, CSAT
≤ 8k input and ≤ 1k output tokens per turn. ≤ $0.05 per conversation... Time to first token p95 ≤ 2 s... Rate limits per IP

traps.evidence: Every answer cites its source, and the bot hands off to a human when it can't answer.
Index public articles only... Visibility filter enforced at query time.
Prompt + RAG. It's reversible, and docs change weekly, which fine-tuning can't keep up with.
Golden eval set and harness in CI... Run on every pull request... Eval regression gate blocks deploys.
One pass only; no agent loop... Reranker model. Pull forward when recall@5 meets target but the top-1 result is often wrong.

note: An exemplary, proportionate RAG plan that avoids every trap, validates risks early with a CI eval harness, and handles grounding, access, injection and operations concretely; its only notable gap is thin total cost/effort estimation.
